outcome: As of 13 Oct 2026 no accepted resolution of the four-dimensional Yang–Mills existence and mass gap problem has appeared: the Clay problem page (opened) still labels it “Unsolved”, and the events since 26 Jan 2024 are one refereed-journal claim for pure SU(N) (Faizal and Shabir, June 2026, reviewed only by an AI referee so far), a set of self-published or conditional Zenodo and arXiv claims (several AI-credited, one withdrawn, one retracted by its author, one self-contradictory), an OpenAI release of two unreviewed manuscripts on the two-dimensional O(3) sigma model (6 Oct 2026, described as a warm-up for Yang–Mills), and finite-lattice formalisations that disclaim the problem.
problem_asks: The frozen statement gives only the title “Yang–Mills existence and mass gap”. The parts below come from the Clay problem statement and the Wikipedia lead, both opened. (1) For every compact simple gauge group G. (2) Existence: a quantum Yang–Mills theory on four-dimensional spacetime R^4 (constructed in Euclidean form and reconstructed), satisfying the standards of constructive quantum field theory (Clay: the Wightman axioms). (3) Nontriviality: the theory is not a trivial (free or Gaussian) one. (4) Mass gap: the theory has a mass gap Δ > 0, i.e. the spectrum above the vacuum is bounded away from zero, so that every particle has strictly positive mass. For G = SU(3) the Wikipedia lead spells (4) as a positive lower bound on glueball masses. Parts (2) to (4) must hold for each G in (1).

events.what_happened: On 6 Oct 2026 OpenAI posted 722 AI-generated manuscripts (372 result families) in its openai/math repository, attributed to an unreleased internal model. Two concern the two-dimensional O(3) nonlinear sigma model: “The canonical massive continuum limit of the two-dimensional O(3) model” and its companion “An Isolated Particle Pole for the Two-Dimensional O(3) Spin Field”, in folders dated 4 Oct 2026. Scientific American reports them under a “Baby Yang-Mills” heading and quotes Michael Douglas calling the sigma model “widely considered the ‘warm-up’ for Yang-Mills”. I could not read either PDF (both the blob and raw views returned compressed binary), so the content below comes from the VibeMathed problem entry and from Scientific American, not from the manuscripts.
events.revisions: Folders dated 4 Oct 2026 (VibeMathed gives solve date 2026-10-04). The repository history.md, dated 7 Oct 2026, lists 14 repaired manuscripts and 3 withdrawals (the Weil-classes, Kuga–Satake and K3 Hodge papers); neither O(3) manuscript is named there.
events.delivers: Per the VibeMathed entry's reading of Theorem 1.2: suitably normalised smeared lattice spins of the nearest-neighbour two-dimensional O(3) model converge in law and in all moments. The limit is reported as interacting (non-Gaussian), reflection positive, reconstructing a local relativistic theory with unique vacuum, and having a Hamiltonian gap. Scope: two dimensions, an O(3) sigma model, not a gauge theory.
events.remains: All of the four-dimensional gauge-theory content: existence of a quantum Yang–Mills theory on R^4 for each compact simple G, its nontriviality as a gauge theory, and a mass gap for it.

checked_by.qualification: NYU mathematician quoted by Scientific American on this release. The article does not say which of the OpenAI papers he read.
checked_by.what_they_did: Read or skimmed some of the release. Said of “the first of these papers”: “both groundbreaking and comprehensible” and “I haven't digested it or understood all the details, but it seems very reasonable”; of the second, “horrible”; of the rest, “incomprehensible slop”. This is not a verification of the O(3) pair.

events.doubts: (1) VibeMathed records the O(3) result as “Candidate (review pending)”, verification “Unreviewed”, publication “Announced”; its “Proved” headline sits beside those status fields. (2) In the same release three manuscripts were withdrawn after a sign error that OpenAI's audit found, and two dependent papers went with them. The O(3) pair is not among the withdrawals, but nothing in my reading shows it was checked for the same kind of error. (3) OpenAI did not include full prompts or run-time details (Scientific American). (4) Bauerschmidt's “slop” remarks concern other papers; no named critic addressed these two.
events.direction: Affirmative for a two-dimensional analogue: the claimed construction of an interacting continuum O(3) sigma model with a mass gap, which the sources call the warm-up for Yang–Mills. It neither bears on nor decides the four-dimensional gauge question.

events.what_happened: consensusframework/yang-mills-mass-gap: a Lean 4 / Mathlib formalisation of finite-volume lattice gauge theory (Wilson action, Gibbs measure, polymer and cluster expansion), released as numbered modules (“Stone 51” to “Stone 57”). The README says it is “not a proof, partial proof or claimed solution of the Yang–Mills Existence and Mass Gap Millennium Problem” and that “nothing here should be cited as a solution or partial solution of the Clay problem”. The README credits many named AI models as coauthors. The releases page shows nine releases from 12 Jul (“v1.0-pre-zulip”) to 11 Oct (“zenodo-v57”); the page does not show years, and 2026 is inferred from the page footer and the Version 50 entry.
events.revisions: Nine releases shown, from v1.0-pre-zulip (12 Jul) to zenodo-v57 (11 Oct); Versions 50 to 57 fall between late Aug and Oct. The README gives the Stone 57 integration on 9 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: Finite-volume, small-β lattice results only: per the README, “every verified result is a finite-lattice theorem”, e.g. cluster-expansion identities, finite-volume covariance decay and Lipschitz stability of polymer functionals.
events.remains: Everything in the continuum problem: the R^4 theory, the continuum or infinite-volume limit, and the mass gap. The README marks the lattice mass-gap target (HasLatticeMassGap) as “stated and explicitly marked open”.
events.time_since_posted: about 3 months (earliest release 12 Jul, year inferred)
events.direction: Does not address the Millennium problem; the README disclaims it. Its results are finite-lattice theorems only.

events.what_happened: Mir Faizal and Arshid Shabir, “Reflection-Positive Construction of a Four-Dimensional SU(N) Yang-Mills Theory with Mass Gap and Confinement”, arXiv:2606.19362 (submitted 9 Jun 2026). Published in Fortschritte der Physik 74(4), e70097 (2026), DOI 10.1002/prop.70097. Starts from a reflection-positive lattice formulation of pure SU(N) Yang–Mills and claims a continuum limit with exponential clustering and a strictly positive string tension, plus a transfer operator with a uniform gap. The arXiv comments say the supporting calculations appear in four separate journal papers, included at the end of this paper; that material is not on the arXiv page. A Pith page hosts an automated review (grok-4.3, read 27 Jun 2026).
events.revisions: arXiv: v1 only. Journal: Fortsch. Phys. 74 (2026) 4, e70097; the journal's acceptance and publication dates were not established.
events.delivers: Claims, for the SU(N) family named in the title, existence of a reflection-positive continuum limit of pure four-dimensional Yang–Mills; exponential clustering and positive string tension in the continuum; independence of the regulator and a unique limit measure (“depends on no special regulator”, “a unique limiting measure”); and a transfer operator with a uniform gap, which is the mass-gap claim. The abstract makes no claim for other compact simple groups.
events.remains: Compact simple groups outside the SU(N) family (SO, Sp, exceptional). Whether the reconstructed theory meets the full Clay formulation, which I could not check because the PDF was unreadable. The gap in physical units, which the continuum argument must carry through.

checked_by.what_they_did: Answered a fixed list of questions. Its one major objection is that “no explicit bound is supplied on per-scale defect size”, and it asks whether gauge-covariant corrections over O(log(1/a)) scales could close the gap or drive the string tension to zero. The page states no human expert has reviewed the paper yet, and its “simulated authors' rebuttal” is generated text.

checked_by.who: Fortschritte der Physik (Wiley), journal of record
checked_by.qualification: A refereed journal, as far as I know; I did not establish its referee process.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (2026, vol. 74, issue 4). The journal page surfaced in search and was not opened.

events.doubts: (1) The only public engagement I found is an automated review. It names a missing explicit per-scale defect bound, which the continuum argument needs. (2) The review says the step that sums small defects across scales lacks visible bounds, and asks whether gauge-covariant corrections accumulate. (3) No human expert comment, erratum or follow-up was found in my searches. (4) A search summary said the arXiv text admits an assumption of uniform bounds on the measures. I could not read the PDF to confirm it, so it is unverified and I have not relied on it.
events.direction: Affirmative for pure SU(N) in four dimensions: claims existence of a continuum theory and a mass gap, via the reflection-positive route.

events.what_happened: John Henry Watt with Claude Opus 4.6 Extended, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Grok 4.20 as listed creators: “The Yang-Mills Mass Gap: From Proof Attempts to Dissolution by Recontextualisation”, Zenodo 19424275 (v3, dated 5 Apr 2026, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19424275). A record with the same title, 19423313, also exists. The abstract says “the mass gap is not a dynamical mystery requiring non-perturbative proof” but “a geometric fact of quantised spacetime”. A search description (not read on the record) lists the claimed results: a solved matrix model with topological spectral gap (Theorems A and B); the first rigorous construction of a mass-gapped four-dimensional gauge theory, on non-commutative R^4_θ; a proof of confinement at all couplings; and a proof sketch of a lattice mass gap at all finite couplings. I read only the abstract and metadata.
events.revisions: v3 dated 5 Apr 2026 (created and modified the same day). Earlier versions were not read. Duplicate-title record 19423313.
events.delivers: Claimed: (a) a matrix-model result (Theorems A and B), which is not the gauge problem; (b) a mass-gapped construction on non-commutative R^4_θ, which is a different theory from the commutative one the problem asks about; (c) confinement at all couplings and a lattice mass-gap sketch, which is a lattice result. The commutative four-dimensional theory for each compact simple G is not what (b) constructs.
events.remains: The commutative R^4 Yang–Mills theory for every compact simple G: existence, nontriviality and mass gap. The lattice sketch is not a continuum result.
events.doubts: The main theory is non-commutative, so it is not the stated problem. The record frames itself as “dissolution by recontextualisation”, which reframes the question rather than answering it as stated. No reviewer. Several same-titled deposits exist.
events.direction: Claims a dissolution of the problem plus claimed results on other theories (matrix model, non-commutative YM, a lattice sketch). Relative to the problem as stated, the claimed object is a different theory, and the lattice part is a different question.
events.object: Per the search description (not read on the record): a claimed mass-gapped construction of non-commutative Yang–Mills on R^4_θ. Whether it is explicit or non-constructive is not stated in what I read.

events.what_happened: Sourav Chatterjee (Stanford), “A scaling limit of SU(2) lattice Yang–Mills–Higgs theory”, arXiv:2401.10507. In any dimension d≥2, constructs a scaling limit of SU(2) lattice Yang–Mills coupled to a Higgs field in the fundamental representation (degenerate potential). The stereographic projection of the gauge field converges to a massive Gaussian field, with mass generated by the Higgs mechanism. The abstract says “the question of constructing a non-Gaussian scaling limit remains open.” Chatterjee also gave a Clay Millennium lecture on this problem on 15 Oct 2025; that is a talk, not a new written result. A later paper (arXiv:2512.00570) cites this one, per a search snippet I did not open.
events.delivers: A Gaussian scaling limit of SU(2) lattice Yang–Mills–Higgs, with mass supplied by the Higgs field, in every dimension d≥2.
events.remains: Pure Yang–Mills (no Higgs field) in four dimensions; a non-Gaussian limit; a positive mass gap for the pure gauge theory; all compact simple G.
events.direction: Neither confirms nor refutes the pure-gauge problem: the Higgs field supplies the mass, so the result is for a different theory.

events.delivers: Claimed existence of a positive mass gap in each component Hilbert space of quantum Yang–Mills fields. The dimension and gauge group are not stated in the part of the abstract I read.
events.remains: Whatever the claimed scope leaves open. Not established from what I read.
events.doubts: A single-author preprint revised over seven versions, with no review found. Scope is unclear from the part of the abstract I read.
events.direction: Claimed affirmative.

events.what_happened: Puskar Mondal, “A Geometric Approach to the Yang-Mills Mass Gap”, arXiv:2301.06996 (v1 17 Jan 2023; v7 12 Nov 2023, current). Abstract: a regularised Bakry–Émery Ricci curvature, if positive, “is shown to produce a mass gap for 2+1 and 3+1 dimensional Yang-Mills theory assuming the existence of a quantized Yang-Mills theory” on Minkowski spacetime.
events.delivers: Conditional: a mass gap in 2+1 and 3+1 dimensions, given (i) positivity of the regularised curvature and (ii) existence of a quantised Yang–Mills theory. It establishes neither.
events.remains: Existence (assumed), the curvature positivity (a hypothesis), and the unconditional four-dimensional result.
events.doubts: The result assumes existence, which is the first half of the problem.
events.direction: Conditional; does not answer either question unconditionally.

events.what_happened: Simone Farinelli, “Renormalized Four Dimensional Quantum Yang-Mills Theory and Mass Gap”, arXiv:1406.4177 (math.GM). v1 16 Jun 2014; v17 27 Mar 2024, the only version after the frozen revision. Abstract: “the spectrum of the corresponding (non-local) QCD Hamilton operator is proven to be positive and bounded away from zero”, positive except for the vacuum.
events.delivers: Claimed: positivity and a gap for the spectrum of a non-local QCD Hamilton operator. Because the operator is non-local, the theory may not be the standard local Yang–Mills Hamiltonian the problem refers to. I did not read the body to check.
events.remains: Whether the non-local operator is the Clay theory; the rest of the Clay formulation.
events.doubts: Posted in math.GM, not refereed. Seventeen versions over ten years, one withdrawn. The operator is non-local, a possible difference from the standard theory.
events.direction: Claimed affirmative, for a non-local operator.

events.what_happened: Simone Farinelli, “Four Dimensional Quantum Yang-Mills Theory for Weak Coupling Strength: Mass Gap Implies Quark Confinement”, arXiv:2406.16881 (v1 16 Apr 2024; v2 30 Jun 2024). Abstract: shows quark confinement “for sufficiently small values of the bare coupling constant, provided the existence of the mass gap”.
events.delivers: Conditional: confinement at small bare coupling, assuming the mass gap. It establishes neither existence nor a mass gap.
events.remains: Existence and the mass gap themselves.
events.doubts: Conditional by its own abstract.
events.direction: Conditional; does not decide the problem.

events.what_happened: Arkady L. Kholodenko, “Gravity assisted solution of the mass gap problem for pure Yang-Mills fields”, arXiv:1001.0029 (v1 30 Dec 2009; v2 3 Aug 2010, “fully revised and updated”). Abstract: “to prove the existence of the mass gap for quantum source-free Yang-Mills (Y-M) fields”.
events.delivers: Claimed: a proof of the mass gap for pure Yang–Mills, by a gravity-assisted method per the title. I read only the abstract.
events.remains: All of it, as claimed.
events.doubts: No peer review found in my searches; the claim has been public since 2009.
events.direction: Claimed affirmative.

events.what_happened: V. Parameswaran Nair, “Towards a Proof of Mass Gap in 3d Yang-Mills Theory”, arXiv:2608.10133 (v1 10 Aug 2026; v2 22 Aug 2026, corrected typos and added a paragraph to the discussion). Abstract: “We give the outlines of a proof for the existence of a mass gap for the 3d Yang-Mills theory”, via an inequality on the eigenvalues of the Laplacian on gauge-invariant configuration space.
events.delivers: An outline of a proof for three-dimensional Yang–Mills. It does not claim the Millennium problem and says nothing about four dimensions.
events.remains: The four-dimensional problem entirely; a complete proof even in three dimensions (only an outline is claimed).
events.doubts: Outline only, by the author's own title (“Towards a Proof”).
events.direction: Affirmative in three dimensions, as an outline; not a four-dimensional result.

events.what_happened: GitHub zhouhm23/yang-mills-3d, described in a search snippet as “Lean 4 formalizations of partial results on the 3D Yang-Mills mass gap problem (work in progress)”, with partial results from ongoing work “attributed to Z.ai”, no paper yet, and a reduction of the remaining problem to two named unproven inputs that are passed to the Lean theorem as hypotheses. The repository returned HTTP 404 when I opened it, so the description rests on the snippet alone.
events.revisions: Unknown; the repository returned 404 when opened.
events.delivers: Per the snippet only: partial three-dimensional results, conditional on two named inputs.
events.remains: The four-dimensional problem and the Clay problem entirely.
events.doubts: The snippet says a proposed cluster criterion was falsified. The page no longer resolves at this URL.
events.direction: Partial, three-dimensional and conditional.

events.what_happened: GitHub merfijang/yang-mills-gap: “Lean 4 blueprint of the Yang–Mills mass gap. AI agents prove lemmas; only proofs accepted by Lean count.” The README says AI agents on yangmills.xyz prove blueprint lemmas, and that “The mass gap itself is NOT solved. Progress means lemmas accepted by the Lean kernel on the way to it.” Nodes are layered foundation, hard, open and boss; the boss-level Millennium problem is “the goal, not a Lean statement”. Accepted proofs may depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, with no sorry. The README credits the first agent that proves a node. The repository shows 52 commits and Lean/Mathlib v4.34.0. The README does not name the agents.
events.revisions: 52 commits. The date of the latest commit was not captured.
events.delivers: Infrastructure: a blueprint and a checker. The README lists no accepted lemma-level result in what I read, and it makes no claim on the mass gap.
events.remains: Every node in the open and boss layers, including the Millennium problem itself.
events.direction: No claim on the problem.

events.what_happened: An OSF preprint (osf.io/preprints/osf/bgu6a) that a search snippet describes as a March 2026 Gribov–Zwanziger construction: “One constructs a gauge-fixed lattice Yang–Mills measure satisfying the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms and establish the existence of a strictly positive mass gap in four dimensions for sufficiently small coupling.” The OSF page returned only the site name when I opened it, so the title, authors and claim come from the snippet.
events.revisions: Unknown.
events.delivers: Per the snippet: a lattice measure with a mass gap for small coupling in four dimensions. It is a lattice result, not a continuum one.
events.remains: The continuum limit, all couplings, and all compact simple G.
events.doubts: Lattice-only by the snippet's own description. I could not read the paper, so the Gribov-horizon argument is unevaluated.
events.direction: Claimed affirmative, but on the lattice at small coupling.

A ResearchGate publication with the same title, 403077786, also turned up; I could not open either page, so I cannot confirm they are the same record. A search snippet of the introduction restates the Clay problem. A secondhand summary of the paper says it argues the gap is not merely a technical challenge and likely needs new mathematical ideas.
events.revisions: Unknown.
events.delivers: Not established: the snippet restates the problem and shows no solution claim. I could not read the paper.
events.remains: Not established.
events.doubts: The listed affiliation is an MBA programme, per a search snippet of the record. Unverified.
events.direction: Not established from what I could read.

A search summary says it claims a complete solution via the Gribov–Zwanziger framework and reports a gap of about 0.5 GeV for SU(3). SSRN returned HTTP 403 to my fetch, so the description rests on search results alone.
events.revisions: Unknown.
events.delivers: Per the search summary only: a claimed complete solution for SU(3) with a numerical gap.
events.remains: Unknown; not read.
events.doubts: Unopened. Search results show no peer review.

events.what_happened: Croft Adams, Medium post “YANG-MILLS EXISTENCE AND MASS GAP: COMPLETE PROOF WRITEUP” (dated Feb 2026 per search results). Per a search excerpt, the central claim is that a trace constraint on the field eigenvalues forces positive energy, so there are “no massless gluons”. The excerpt asserts a bound of about 0.866 times a field norm on the largest eigenvalue without derivation, and a gap Δ = (1 − C₄)·Λ_QCD without deriving it. A companion post is said to describe a 636-line Lean 4 file, which I did not find. Medium returned HTTP 403 to my fetch.
events.revisions: Unknown.
events.delivers: Claimed (per excerpt): a mass gap via “no massless gluons” in four dimensions.
events.remains: The key eigenvalue bound, which the excerpt asserts without proof.
events.doubts: On my reading of the excerpt, the step from the zero-sum trace condition to an eigenvalue bound is asserted, and the link from eigenvalues to the energy functional is not shown. The post is single-author with no review.
events.direction: Claimed affirmative, per the excerpt.

events.what_happened: Anthropic's Science-blog post of 25 Sep 2026 reports that Claude computed the nine-loop MHV six-particle amplitude in planar N=4 super Yang–Mills, one loop past the previous record. Lance Dixon's addendum says “Claude had computed the nine-loop MHV six-particle amplitude in planar N=4 super Yang-Mills” and that he “checked Claude's nine-loop result” and “validated the result independently”. The post also says Song He's group reached most of a concurrent result with GPT-6 assistance. The post does not mention the Yang–Mills mass gap or the Clay problem. This is a different theory that shares the name, recorded as a discounted event.
events.revisions: None found.
events.delivers: Discounted: amplitudes in N=4 supersymmetric Yang–Mills, a toy theory. It establishes nothing about existence or the mass gap of pure Yang–Mills in four dimensions.
events.remains: All of the Clay problem.

checked_by.qualification: Held the prior eight-loop record in this computation, per the post.

disputes.summary: AI systems are credited as co-creators or coauthors on several Yang–Mills deposits, with no account of which contributions are load-bearing. The Watt deposits (19322773, 19412061, 19424275) list Claude Opus 4.6 Extended, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Grok 4.20; only 19424275's abstract gives an account (“Using adversarial AI collaboration across three frontier models…”). The consensusframework README names fifteen AI models as coauthors for finite-lattice results and says a human coordinator is “not the sole author”. Recorded, not resolved.

summary: Nothing I could open shows an accepted resolution of the four-dimensional problem, and the Clay problem page (opened) still labels it “Unsolved”, saying “no proof of this property is known”. The Wikipedia lead (opened; the fetched version was last edited 6 Aug 2026) gives Yang–Mills no status tag, while its navigation box tags Poincaré as solved and Navier–Stokes as “solution claimed”. The events fall into four groups. (i) The closest call is Faizal and Shabir (arXiv 9 Jun 2026; Fortschritte der Physik 74(4), 2026), a claimed reflection-positive continuum construction and mass gap for pure SU(N). Its only public review I found is an automated one, which flags a missing explicit per-scale defect bound. I did not verify the journal's refereeing, and the claim covers SU(N) only; a reader who weights the journal acceptance heavily would count it as a restricted claim, while one who weights the missing bound would not. (ii) AI-credited deposits by John Henry Watt (Zenodo 19322773, 19412061, 19424275) list Claude Opus 4.6 Extended, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Grok 4.20 as co-creators. Their claims rest on non-standard theories (non-commutative Yang–Mills), are conditional, or are a claimed reframing. The 19424275 abstract is the only authors' account of AI use I found on any of them. (iii) OpenAI's 6 Oct 2026 release includes two manuscripts on the two-dimensional O(3) nonlinear sigma model, which Scientific American calls “Baby Yang-Mills” and the warm-up for it. The result is for a two-dimensional analogue, has no review (VibeMathed: Candidate, review pending), and is attributed to “an unreleased internal OpenAI model”, a credit made in a README about the whole release. I could not read the manuscripts, so I cannot say whether they claim more than the VibeMathed entry reports. (iv) Solo or conditional preprints since 2009 (Kholodenko, Mondal, Lim, Farinelli twice, Chishtie, Jacobsen, Agawa, Chatterjee, Silva-Filho twice, Ross, Nitu, Nair), plus a Lean lattice formalisation (consensusframework) that names fifteen AI models and disclaims the problem. Jacobsen (2025) was withdrawn by arXiv Admin; Agawa (2025) was retracted by its author as a hypothesis; Chishtie's mass-gap claim appears in v2 but not in the current v5 abstract; Silva-Filho's trilogy calls itself unconditional while its mass-gap result rests on a stated hypothesis. Not recorded as events for this problem: the Anthropic nine-loop N=4 result (recorded as a discounted event above), OpenAI's Navier–Stokes claim of 8 Sep 2026 (a different problem), and the Chatterjee lecture of 15 Oct 2025 (a talk). Several items are unverified secondary reports and are not recorded as events: a prediction market, a reported OpenAI statement that it would not claim the prize, Hacker News speculation about the OpenAI advisory panel, and an X rumour that Claude had worked on a Millennium problem (a Navier–Stokes claim, with Yang–Mills among the guesses). Clay's prize rules were not opened; a secondary explainer says a claimed solution must be published and then stand two years before the Clay committee considers it. Dates for deposits with several versions are the earliest dates I could establish, and in several cases the first version was not read.
competing_reading: The strongest case for reading the record differently: (a) Faizal and Shabir is the only claim in a refereed journal for the pure-gauge core of the problem. If refereeing counts, the problem has a restricted claimed resolution (SU(N)) that would be the most substantive progress in the record, and the judging pass would weigh the referee process more than the AI review. (b) The OpenAI O(3) pair is the most credible AI-attributed mathematics in this area in these sources: it comes from the developer's own repository and carries a “Proved” label. A literal reading of Scientific American's “the equivalent of the Yang–Mills problem for this simpler model” could count it as AI progress on the problem; the scope reading says it is a two-dimensional analogue that settles nothing about gauge theory in four dimensions. (c) The Watt deposits credit three AI models as co-creators and describe “adversarial AI collaboration”, which a generous reading takes as AI involvement in the substantive mathematics; the narrower reading says the record does not state any load-bearing contribution, and that the claims are on other theories or are conditional.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The text of the two OpenAI O(3) manuscripts, which I could not read: whether either makes a claim about four-dimensional gauge theory, what the attribution says beyond the release README, and whether any Lean formalisation covers them. (2) Referee reports, acceptance date and any published comment on Faizal and Shabir; a readable PDF to check the assumptions and the claimed series of journal papers. (3) Expert verification or refusal of the Faizal and Shabir argument, especially the per-scale defect bound. (4) The earliest version and the author's own description of load-bearing AI contributions for the Watt deposits, and a build of their Lean files to check the sorry-free and axiom claims. (5) Version histories for Silva-Filho's trilogy and for Chishtie's arXiv:2505.09947 v1 to v4, to date when the mass-gap claim entered and left. (6) The Clay Institute's problem page at a later date, and any change to the Wikipedia status line.

events.ai_basis: Claude had computed the nine-loop MHV six-particle amplitude in planar N=4 super Yang-Mills.

judgement.why: The statement asks for 4D quantum Yang–Mills existence with a mass gap for every compact simple group. Faizal–Shabir claims only SU(N), so at most a case; it was published in Fortschritte der Physik, which I counted as a journal of record, but I set it aside as not_credible because several signals line up: a landmark claim with no human uptake in four months, Clay and later 2026 work still treating the problem as open, a physics-journal venue outside constructive QFT, and the automated review flagging the continuum step the problem is known to resist. Jacobsen and Agawa are knocked down (withdrawn/retracted). The many self-published whole-problem claims (Silva-Filho, Chishtie, Ross, Wilson, Croft Adams, and pre-snapshot Lim, Farinelli, Kholodenko) are not_credible. Conditional reductions and formalisations are none; 2D O(3), 3D, Higgs, lattice-only, non-commutative and N=4 results are variants. The O(3) and nine-loop events earn generated AI roles from their own quotes but are variants; Watt and consensusframework AI listings say nothing about what the models produced, so none.
judgement.doubts: Faizal–Shabir is the close call: a reader weighting journal acceptance could make it credible/doubtful, which would give a partial (SU(N)) tier; the Wiley page was not opened and refereeing was not established. Chatterjee (19 Jan 2024) precedes the snapshot by a week. Wilson is year-only 2024 and cannot be placed.
judgement.by: judging pass (JUDGE.md), claude-opus-5-5; not the researching agent and not a human reviewer
